title: Catholic Charities Thanksgiving Meal Kits Run Short as Demand Jumps 50%
excerpt: More than 600 people called Catholic Charities in a single week asking about Thanksgiving meal kits — and the need is growing faster than the help available. The organization handed out 350 kits this year, down from 500 last year, while estimated demand rose about 50 percent.
content:
More than 600 people called Catholic Charities in a single week asking about Thanksgiving meal kits — and the need is growing faster than the help available.

The organization handed out 350 kits this year, down from 500 last year, because of limited funding, while estimated demand rose about 50 percent compared with previous years, Catholic Charities said.

Each kit carried a turkey, stuffing, potatoes and other holiday essentials for families who had signed up in advance. Ashley Guajardo waited almost 50 minutes in the car line to pick up a kit for her mother-in-law, and said the long line itself showed the need: “Definitely, you can see by the amount of people that are looking for places that are donating food, that are donating things for the holidays. So you see the need when you see more people.”

Magdanela Parra, who picked up a kit for her household, said her family can afford only basic food, and that every year feels harder and more expensive than the last.

Edgar Martinez with Catholic Charities said he believes the organization received more funding last year. More than 10 students from San Agustin High School volunteered at the distribution, and the organization’s next food drive is in April.

With more than 600 calls in a single week and only 350 kits available, demand outran supply this Thanksgiving.

Sources: Catholic Charities Thanksgiving meal kit distribution, Nov. 18, 2026.
